title: Obserra Data Protection Compliance Crosswalk
scopeStatement: This Obserra-authored crosswalk maps technical and governance safeguards to auditable implementation evidence. It supports assurance and audit preparation but does not constitute legal advice, certification, or a regulator determination.

controls.capability: Data handled by identity, commerce, governance, SaaS, and export services is bounded by explicit schemas and classified by operational purpose.
Application routes process only the identity, entitlement, purchase, operational, and audit attributes required for the transaction.
Purchase, entitlement, recovery, export, and audit data are associated with documented operational purposes and bounded request contracts.
Sensitive governance, billing, containment, and export actions require authenticated identity, owner authorization, and recent reverification.
External provider, control-plane, and browser communications use HTTPS endpoints with platform-managed TLS.
Provider credentials and control-plane tokens are read from environment configuration and are not returned in application responses.
Session revocations, tokens, audit operations, and temporary exports use bounded identifiers, expiration controls, or documented retention contracts.
Session, token, and organization containment mechanisms revoke access without waiting for normal token expiration.
Operational logs use bounded references and sanitized outcomes while excluding card data, secrets, and raw authentication credentials.
Governance PDF and Excel exports require recent reverification, documented purpose, owner authorization, no-store delivery, and durable export audit records.
Webhook signatures, idempotency keys, signed entitlement tokens, and audience binding protect transaction and authorization integrity.
Release gates, cross-target validation, rollback evidence, and bounded provider timeouts reduce data-service disruption and uncontrolled recovery risk.
Runtime errors, security findings, release outcomes, containment operations, and audit exports produce evidence suitable for incident investigation.
Stripe, Clerk, Resend, Vercel, and control-plane integrations are accessed through bounded provider contracts with timeout and fail-closed handling.
The Compliance Compiler continuously derives evidence-based control status, freshness, gaps, and remediation priorities without allowing AI to invent compliance evidence.
